question: What is the main purpose of connecting nurses through international organizations?

options.A: To create a unified voice for the profession
options.B: To recruit nurses away from developing nations
options.C: To replace local nursing councils entirely
options.D: To set identical salaries for all countries

explanation: Global nursing bodies bring together different workforces to speak with one strong, shared voice on health issues. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why do nursing practices differ between countries despite shared core values?

options.A: International bodies forbid uniform practices worldwide
options.B: Local resources and cultures shape how care is delivered
options.C: Basic nursing values change constantly across regions
options.D: Different countries use entirely different human biology

explanation: While core values remain the same everywhere, the actual environment, funding, and culture of a country change daily practice. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h1)

question: Who makes up the membership of the International Council of Nurses?
explanation: ICN operates as a federation made up of professional associations representing nurses from individual countries. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a primary focus area for the ICN?

options.A: Ensuring quality nursing care for everyone
options.B: Setting individual hospital staff shift rosters
options.D: Advocating for sound global health policies

explanation: ICN works at a high policy and professional level, leaving local staff rostering to individual hospitals and local managers. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h2)

question: How do global standards help countries with developing health systems?

options.A: They supply direct funding for building new hospitals
options.B: They eliminate the need for local licensing exams
options.C: They provide clear benchmarks to elevate local training programs
options.D: They force countries to abandon their traditional practices

explanation: Global guidelines give emerging nations a proven framework to model their nursing education and clinical safety protocols after. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h3)

question: A Nigerian nurse plans to migrate and practice abroad. Why are international educational standards helpful in this situation?

options.A: They automatically grant a license without further testing
options.B: They guarantee a higher salary in the destination country
options.C: They translate local Nigerian textbooks into foreign languages
options.D: They ensure basic competencies are recognized across borders

explanation: Common global standards make it easier for regulatory bodies to evaluate the training background of migrating nurses. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is a major workforce advocacy goal of international nursing organizations?

options.A: Reducing the length of basic nursing training
options.B: Eliminating the need for continuing education
options.C: Limiting the number of students admitted to schools
options.D: Pushing for safe staffing levels and fair pay

explanation: Global nursing bodies constantly campaign for proper compensation and safe work environments to protect practitioners. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why do international bodies insist that nurses take part in health policy-making?

options.A: Nursing laws are too complex for non-nurses to read
options.B: Policy tables require a large number of physical occupants
options.C: Governments lack the budget to hire outside policy consultants
options.D: Those closest to patient care understand what systems need to work

explanation: Nurses experience clinical realities firsthand, making their input vital when designing health policies that actually function. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why does the WHO rely heavily on international nursing organizations?

options.A: Nursing bodies fund the majority of WHO research programs
options.B: Nurses control all international hospital budgets
options.C: WHO has no internal staff trained in medicine
options.D: Nurses make up the largest segment of the health workforce

explanation: Because nurses form the bulk of healthcare providers worldwide, WHO must collaborate with them to reach global health goals. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of reports like the State of the World's Nursing?

options.A: To advertise nursing schools to high school students
options.B: To provide data that encourages governments to invest in nursing
options.C: To rank individual nurses by clinical test scores
options.D: To punish countries with nursing shortages

explanation: These reports offer clear statistics on workforce numbers and needs, helping advocates lobby governments for better funding and support. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which body connects Nigerian nursing standards to international benchmarks?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN acts as the regulatory body that connects local Nigerian training and practice with recognised international standards. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h6)

question: How does participation in international nursing forums directly help Nigerian nurses?

options.A: By providing free housing for every nurse in the country
options.B: By automatically stopping all nurses from traveling abroad
options.C: By bringing home new ideas on curriculum reform and advanced practice
options.D: By replacing local nursing exams with foreign tests

explanation: Exposing local leaders to global practices helps them update Nigerian training programs and expand professional roles. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h6)
